name: Himmel
description: A managed, orchestrated harness for running Claude Code as a safe, repeatable agent: hooks, guardrails, slash commands, a Jira CLI, and a cross-session handover system.

paragraphs: 🚀 New here? → Getting Started: from clone to your first PR-gated loop in about 15 minutes. Deciding whether it is worth it? Read Why himmel, the failure modes it exists for and what each one costs. Want the design in one read? System design explains the parts, one ticket's flow, the trust model and the trade-offs. Want the wiring? Architecture draws the enforcement layers, handover, fleet, Jira seam and observability chain.

himmel is a development engine for a solo operator or a small team who works with Claude Code every day. It wraps Claude Code in hooks, guardrails, slash commands, a local Jira CLI and a handover system, so the work follows a worktree-isolated, PR-gated, Jira-tracked workflow without anyone having to remember the rules.

The idea is simple: anything you would otherwise repeat by hand (checking a commit, reviewing a PR, writing down where you stopped, restarting after a usage cap) becomes a tool or a gate. Safety comes from structure, not from Claude remembering a paragraph of instructions.
features: Every feature has one doc that owns its detail; the full map is docs/README.md.
Pre-commit and Claude tool-call guardrail hooks, and the multi-agent PR
